answer.line: Gap junctions are channels that join two cytoplasms, so ions pass straight across. That is how heart cells beat as one.

steps: Match the job. Passing directly from cytoplasm to cytoplasm needs a channel through both membranes.
In animal cells that channel is the gap junction, built from connexons.
Heart cells pack gap junctions into their intercalated discs, so the action potential spreads from cell to cell.

choices.note: A hemidesmosome anchors a cell to the basement membrane below it, not to a neighbor cell.
Connexon channels: ions walk straight from one cell into the next.
Tight junctions seal the space between cells so nothing leaks through. They do not join the cytoplasms.
Plasmodesmata do this exact job, but through plant cell walls. Cardiac muscle is animal tissue.
Desmosomes are rivets that hold cells together under stress. Heart discs have them too, but nothing passes through.

lockIt: Gap junctions pass, tight junctions seal, desmosomes rivet, hemidesmosomes anchor.

The gap junction is outlined as the answer.
